cues: Stemma's derived Serialize still emits entry_index, owner_index, bindings and owned_visits in hash order; to_snapshot is the canonical form and the only one mere reads

entries, visits and owners are written in slot order, which follows insertion only until a deletion frees a slot; stable under the kernel's hydrate-and-write cycle, not canonical for a long-lived Stemma
nothing in chartulary forbids or counts a second bearer at admission; commit_bearing_batch guards only a node bearing its own graph

a nested graph archived by the earlier first-bearer behaviour with another bearer still live is indistinguishable from an interrupted removal, so recover_archived_bearings would still remove that bearer
EditSpec::RemoveNode through commit_batch removes a bearing node without archiving its nested graph; only remove_bearing_node archives
the digest is over each entry's canonical serde encoding, so a type that serializes a set in hash order (a HashSet, as Container.tags did) must serialize it sorted; muniment sorts maps only
the digest binds entries only: a journal later compacted or rebased would have to carry the digest of the prefix it dropped; muniment's Journal has no compaction today
chartulary's mismatch is StoreError::Codec like its other refusals; a matchable variant would be an API change to the public StoreError enum
prefix_digest costs a linear encode-and-hash of the prefix on every checkpointed open and every checkpoint write, far less than the replay it guards
chartulary still refuses a legacy (assertion-less) snapshot past the journal with an error; it is outside the replay-past rule and only matters when such a snapshot is ahead
Pandect's open reads graph.json and facets.json twice (the hash check, then the decode); the stores are the session's own, so the gap between the reads is not a threat in the stated model
